# Returning to Anicca should not mean guessing

*Anicca build note · Source review from October 19, 2026; status checked October 22, 2026*

Imagine reinstalling an app you already use. You tap Restore Purchases, wait, and cannot tell what happened. Did the request fail? Is your access still being checked? Should you tap again?

That uncertainty is a small product problem worth taking seriously.

Anicca is an iPhone app for daily affirmations and gentle self-care reminders. Its purpose is to make room for a kinder moment in your day. The screens around that experience should also be clear, including the screen you see when something goes wrong.

## A returning customer needs an answer

A review of Anicca's upgrade-screen source found a gap in the code examined. The Restore Purchases action could record an error while the available subscription plans were still empty. But the place that displayed that error existed only in the version of the screen with plans loaded.

The result, at the code level, was a failure message with nowhere to appear in the empty-plan view. This was found through source review and regression checks, rather than a verified customer incident.

The proposed change gives the existing error message a shared place on the screen. It is intended to remain visible whether plans have loaded or not. The patch leaves the purchase and restore functions unchanged; it changes where an existing error message is presented.

## The lesson is about the way back in

An upgrade screen serves people who are deciding whether to subscribe. It also serves people trying to return to something they already paid for. Both deserve a clear response to a tap.

Checks of the proposed source change cover the error-message placement for both screen states. They also check that retrying clears the previous message and that the existing success condition stays intact.

This remains a source-tested proposal. It has not been verified in a native build or an installed or released app. The actual iPhone layout, accessibility behavior and restore flow still need native testing. There is no measured customer or conversion result to report.

The practical goal is straightforward: when a restore attempt fails, show the existing explanation where the person can find it. A calm experience includes knowing what happened.

[View Anicca on the App Store](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/daily-affirmations-anicca/id6755129214). This note describes proposed development work, not a verified release.

## Source and verification scope

The [reviewed paywall source](https://github.com/Daisuke134/life-manager/blob/baac8c681314edd1fc430199f30da410d31a4c1c/apps/mobile/anicca-ios/aniccaios/Onboarding/PaywallVariantBView.swift) shows the empty-plan branch, the existing error presentation, and the restore handler. A read of the canonical source on October 22 found the same file content. The proposal passed 14 source checks on October 19; these inspect code structure and do not execute Swift, RevenueCat, or an iPhone screen. This is an AI-assisted development note, not evidence of improved customer outcomes.

## FAQ

### What was wrong with the Restore Purchases screen?

A source review found that a Restore Purchases error could be recorded while the subscription plans were still empty, but the place that displayed that error existed only in the version of the screen with plans loaded. The failure message had nowhere to appear in the empty-plan view. It was found through source review and regression checks, not a verified customer incident.

### Does the change alter how purchase or restore works?

No. The patch leaves the purchase and restore functions unchanged. It gives the existing error message a shared place on the screen so it stays visible whether plans have loaded or not.

### Has the fix been released in the iPhone app?

Not yet verified. It is a source-tested proposal that passed 14 source checks on October 19; it has not been verified in a native build or an installed or released app, and there is no measured customer or conversion result to report.
